title: Malicious Firefox extensions impersonate popular crypto wallets
content_md: Socket’s threat researchers found three malicious Firefox extensions that impersonated the Phantom, Jupiter, and Bitget crypto wallets. Once installed, the malicious extensions stole recovery phrases and private keys, which would provide the attacker with full control of a wallet. A crypto wallet is an app, browser extension, or physical device that lets you manage cryptocurrency such as Bitcoin. Despite its name, it doesn’t actually hold your coins. Those are recorded on a blockchain , a shared digital record of transactions. Instead, the wallet manages the secret digital keys that let you access and spend them. When you create a wallet, you may be given a recovery phrase: a list of words you can use to restore access. Write it down and store it offline. It’s a backup of your keys, not just an ordinary password. Anyone who gets hold of it can take control of your funds, which is why fake wallet extensions try to steal it. Cybercriminals listed three fake wallet extensions on Firefox Add-ons, impersonating Phantom, Jupiter, and Bitget. The genuine wallets offer extensions for other browsers: Jupiter lists Chrome, Brave, and Edge; Bitget’s extension is for Chrome; and Phantom says its Firefox extension is no longer supported . The malicious extensions looked for 12-, 15-, 18-, and 24-word recovery phrases, as well as Ethereum and Solana private keys.
